title: The letters of the mind
hookLine: a lesson that starts on the board and ends up inside: in the Patti, each school letter becomes a lesson for the soul

lines: A LESSON THAT LEAVES THE CLASSROOM.
cards: Some school lessons never stay at school. A teacher draws a number line on the board, and years later someone waiting on test results counts the days along it in their head.
A coach says keep your eye on the ball, and it turns into advice about a marriage. The lesson leaves the classroom and moves inside.
The Patti does that on purpose, letter after letter, and it says who the real student is.

teach.b: Start with the Patti's center line, its Rahao. It speaks to one pupil, and the pupil is the mind. In paraphrase: why do you forget, foolish mind?
So the slate isn't really on a desk. It's inside. Now watch three letters turn a school lesson into a lesson for the soul.
In paraphrase: when the hair turns white, bright without any soap, the messengers of death arrive and bind you in the chains of Maya.
Guru Nanak makes the letter about gray hair in the mirror, and what it's quietly teaching. Dadai, the letter D.
In paraphrase: I blame no one else; the blame lies in my own deeds. Whatever I did, that I received. Don't blame other people.
On a school board, D is a shape to copy. In the mind, it's the hardest lesson there is: to stop pointing outward first.
Tatai, a hard T. In paraphrase: why put on a show, mortal? In a moment, any moment, you may have to get up and go.
Don't gamble your life away; run to the Lord's shelter. A child learns that letter by tracing it. The mind learns it by remembering it isn't staying forever.
A school lesson is about the letter.
A soul's lesson is about the one learning it. The Patti keeps both: you still learn your letters, but each comes with a question for whoever holds the pen.

how: In kirtan and katha the Patti is sung and explained stanza by stanza, and teachers draw out the inner lesson each letter carries, so a Gurmukhi letter becomes a reminder about the mind.

games.q: what does “the letters of the mind” mean?
o: the first letters a child learns to trace
a secret code only the Gurus could read
school letters turned into lessons for the soul

games.q: letters of the mind — tap the pairs.
p: why do you forget, foolish mind?
blame no one; the fault is my deeds
why put on a show? you must go

s: the Patti's Rahao speaks to a schoolchild
it speaks to the mind: why do you forget, foolish mind?
the dadai stanza says whatever I did, that I received
I blame no one else; the blame lies in my own deeds.

games.q: something has gone wrong, and you're about to explain whose fault it is. what does the letter dadai say?
o: blame the one who started it.
blame no one; look at my own deeds.
games.why: dadai: I blame no one else; the blame lies in my own deeds. whatever I did, that I received.

practice: Think of something you learned as a child, share, look both ways, measure twice, and hold it as it was first taught.

Then ask it the Patti's kind of question, what is this teaching the mind and not just the hands, so look both ways might become pause before I speak, and let one answer come without pushing for a clever one.
If you pray, say Waheguru on the out-breath.

wordCard.voice: The letters of the mind. In the Patti, each letter turns a school lesson into a lesson for the soul, and the student the Rahao speaks to is the mind. Today's word.

orig.note: man: the mind, the inner self; the pupil the Patti's Rahao calls out to.

carryVoice: Your line: the soul's lessons. Kakai, dadai, tatai: three letters, one pupil, the mind. On we go.
